So, you have watched to many episodes of "Mr.Robot"? And now you wish to feel as hacker for a while? So you are in correct place.

This little game (~ 10h) is probably the best hacking simulator. And because of that it has its pros and cons... For example you will have to type commands and read manuals (like hackers do). If you are not afraid, then play.

Fun, short game where you manage executing different attacks to bring down your targets, and snoop around files to find weaknesses in secuity. Story was interesting. Comic relief could be found in some of the non-important private files/logs you come across. Sometimes game wouldn't register clicks or would lag a bit, and made controls a bit clunky in some of the race-against-the-clock parts, but I found no other bugs or issues. I'd reccommend the DLC if you complete the base game and decide you want more, since it basically just re-uses the same mechanics (with some new features) in a new storyline independent from the base game.

Hacknet is a surprisingly fleshed out game, and the experience really makes you feel like you've learned something new. You start off as a script kiddie, but over the course of time the game becomes more reflex-based, with fast typing and memorization playing key roles. All-in-all, probably the best "Hacker Sim" I could ever find, and definitely a game I'll play again.

One of the very few games that I really enjoyed in Steam.

A story about a hacker known as "Bit" which will intrigue you as you try to do his unfinished business for him.

You'll be hacking pc/devices old fashion style: using command lines like what you'll use in HP-UX, also similar to appledos, msdos, and other old OSes. 

A very nostalgic experience before the GUI/mouse...feeling comfortably at home with the >_ (prompt) of yesteryears where the crt/kbd were the norm and the mouse is just a house pest. In this game you are using computers with limited base memory similar to maybe late 70's/early 80's so you can't use all your hacking tools at once.

PRO:
- Has a good story.
- The music is nice and well suited to the game.
- While hacking you can read some funny events/jokes in irc chat logs.
- Has achievements (very achievable and not tied to DLCs).
- Has trading cards.

CONS:
- The base game is rather short.
- Some bug in the command line, but not a game breaker (just use the "TAB key" instead when you encounter it). 
- Leans more to aracde-like than a simulation of real hacking (but the essence is there).

Highly Recommended: for gamer who wants a glimpse of hacking (arcade-like), especially for Older gamers specially those who are familiar/comfortable with the command line and UNIX-like commands and also for achievement perfectionists.

I picked up Hacknet while it was free on Humble, and I have to say, if I had the money to go back and buy it I'd do it a hundred times. Hacknet is a beautiful game with a satisfying story, and it's chock full of easter eggs and tiny details that make it feel like you're actually part of the digial world this all takes place in. The game feels alive; it feels like you're actually breaking into systems people use on a day to tay basis. You'll find personal documents, corporate memos, IRC logs, humurous writing assignments, and much more scattered around the different machines, making it feel like there's an actual world here.

Admittedly, Hacknet does dumb down the hacking a fair bit, making it feel more like you're in CSI rather than a real hackerman. But this is fine. It's a game, it's not meant to be hyperrealistic and super challenging to learn. It doesn't take years of training and a cybersecurity certificationton pick up Hacknet. Additionally, what Hacknet lacks in realism, it more than makes up for in terms of interesting and challenging missions. There's so much to do, so many interesting surprises, and a healthy balance of comedic contracts like stealing fried chicken recipies with some rather serious moral choices. And as if that wasn't enough, many of its missions left me on the edge of my seat, sighing in relief as I [i]barely[/i] hit the mark with merely seconds to spare.

To top it off, Hacknet features a brilliant OST that I just can't stop listening to. Every song was carefully chosen to match the current atmosphere in the game, and it certainly shows. It really feels like you're in a movie here; when that email comes in and the song changes, you [u]know[/u] it's about to go down. 

Overall, Hacknet (and its Labyrinths DLC, which I also highly recommend) is one of the best games I've played. It features a compelling story that will rope you in, even if you aren't its main character. It will play with your emotions quite beautifully, and leave you victorious yet bittersweet. It's such a fascinating, well-designed and well-written game, and it left me begging for more.

This game is fun. Note, I didn't say realistic. It's a hacking game, and like every other hacking game (except some CTFs, but those are more competitions than games) it takes many liberties to make it actually fun for most people. I like it; even as someone who occasionally participates in CTFs, it's fun to chill and absorb myself in this game's fictional world of downloading exploits from 1337 hax0rs and hacking the mainframe. But it still has some ties to realism, for example the notion of getting into one device through another (ex. one mission has you get access to someone's laptop by exploting their phone). Plus, you can substitute some of its easy to remember fake commands for real ones (probe => nmap, forget others but I think there are more).
Buy this.

First, I want to say this game is awesome.  It's much better than hacker evolution and felt more like a spiritual successor to an old game called Uplink.  If you don't know what those games are, it doesn't matter.  This game is the best hacking simulator I've ever played and actually got me interested in learning more outside of the game.

The gameplay involves hacking into different computers and devices by using a set of exploits that you expand upon as you progress through the game.  You don't have to know anything about hacking to get started.  You will quickly learn the basics and as the game progresses, you begin to rely more on your problem solving and creativity to get by.

The game's story unravels as a mystery.  As you play, you continue to follow a series of breadcrumbs.  This is what drives you to keep going in addition to what the next hacking challenge will be.  How far are you willing to go into the rabbit hole?

I also highly recommend getting the Labyrinths DLC.  It is more of a challenge than what you experience in the base game and if you already beat the base game, it will give you that little something extra you might be looking for.
